objective: Design proposal 01 of 4, second round: L'Instrument, a package manager for Arch as a precision instrument. Two 1600x1000 dark screens (loaded and quiet), the FigCraft source, and the rationale.

inputs.tokens: the design-system tokens taken as they are: anthracite #111418, shell white #F7F3ED, muted #A1A6AD, slate #667085, signal orange 100 #FFE5D2 / 300 #FF8E40 / base #FF6A00 / 700 #C95400, royal blue 300 #87A0F4 / base #4169E1
inputs.derivation_rule: no hue outside the tokens was invented: the anodised plates are the anthracite ground with the slate token laid over it; the grain is a slate noise effect blended overlay; the phosphor is the signal-orange token, used only where a reading is live

the_decision.the_arrangement: one milled faceplate read from the top down in full-width bands: header, source bank, control strip, readout window, specification nameplate, record tape. No left column, no right card, no bottom bar.
the_decision.the_two_axes: the seven sources are a horizontal bank of seven equal apertures, each stating its kind (BIN/SRC/SBX/ONE/CRATE/NODE/GIT) and its count; the three functions are one rotary knob in a control bay on the right, with a phosphor pointer thrown at a detent on an engraved scale
the_decision.the_delta: the pending size of each package is a bar on a shared calibrated scale (0-128 MiB) with an end-marker and the exact figure in a column, not a sentence
the_decision.the_detail: the specification of the selection is a full-width nameplate of engraved cells under the window, not a card beside it
the_decision.the_record: the backend's own output is a perforated paper tape emerging from a slot at the bottom: the product's command on one line, what the backend actually ran on the next
the_decision.the_empty_region: the readout window in the quiet screen, on purpose: the instrument's dial with nothing to read; the recess, the engraved grid and the row rules stay visible, and the nameplate names the channel instead of a package
the_decision.the_keyboard: off the surface entirely; a help overlay behind one engraved ? disc in the header

what_was_built.generator: build.py (emits build.jsonl; every layer is a figcraft command)

how: both PNGs were rendered and read back seven times: the knob's radial gradient had its axis on the diagonal and painted a band across the disc; twenty-eight separate knurl vectors did not render; the action buttons were positioned by multiplying each button's own width by its index; the delta figure and its unit were drawn at the same right edge; the density legend collided with the SIZE heading inside the window; the quiet screen's nameplate overflowed its cells

artefacts.note: the rationale: arrangement, budget, the empty region, material, motion, second pass

rules_kept: the Calix application code was not opened, the running application was not started, and no screenshot of it was looked for
the first round's four images in evidence/design-proposals/*.png were not opened
known_gaps: the fonts are system fonts (IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Sans Condensed, IBM Plex Mono); a render on a machine without them falls back
royal blue is not on either screen: the phosphor is the signal-orange token, used only where a reading is live, and a second accent would dilute that
the compact list is shown as an engraved legend of its row shape beside the knob, not drawn as a screen
the help overlay the ? disc opens is not part of this proposal
